title: Event proxy detector & typed sanitizer for telemetry ingestion
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem: The console backend's usage analytics pipeline occasionally accepts malformed or subtly drifting telemetry events that later cause metric gaps, incorrect cost allocation, and noisy downstream alerts. Current validators reject only gross schema violations and offer poor observability for soft-drift (type changes, optional fields appearing with different shapes).

Goal: Implement an "event proxy detector" and a lightweight "typed sanitizer" stage in the ingest path that together: 1) detect soft schema drift at high throughput with low added latency, 2) apply deterministic, auditable type coercions/enrichments for common, safe mismatches, 3) emit enriched telemetry and drift signals to observability (metrics + eval logs) and 4) provide a canary replay and rollback story for new sanitizer rules.

Scope: Backend service changes only (ingest sidecar + validation library + control flags). No UI work in this ticket. Key features: 
- Event Proxy Detector: probabilistic matcher that tags events as "ok", "soft-drift", or "reject" using a lightweight signature+schema hash plus statistical type checks. Runs as an inline gRPC filter in the Console-ingest service.
- Typed Sanitizer: pluggable rules (coercion, defaulting, normalization) with a provenance header added to events describing transformations. Rules include numeric string -> int/float, timestamp normalization, enumerated string normalization (lowercase/alias map), and nested object flattening for the top-k known fields.
- Drift Telemetry: counters and histograms per route/model/tenant for drift rate, sanitization rate, rejection rate, and latency impact. Sampled example events (before/after) forwarded to the telemetry-eval topic for downstream human review.
- Canary + Rollback: feature-flagged rollout via runtime config (console-config service). Support replaying sanitized and raw events into a staging pipeline for parity checks before enabling in production.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Added end-to-end latency <= +6ms p50 on ingest path when detector + sanitizer enabled (measure against baseline).
- Sanitizer correctness tests with >95% coverage for rule set and deterministic provenance header format.
- Drift alerts created when soft-drift rate > 2% over a 15m window for any tenant or route.
- Playbook and runbook update with steps to rollback sanitizer rules and to run canary replays.

Security & Compliance: rules must not drop PII fields. Sanitizer must preserve original payload in a replayable topic for audit. Security review required (KMS key usage for any stored examples).
comments: 2026-02-14: Triage: flagged as P0 due to recurring billing/metrics incidents tied to malformed usage events. Assigned to Mahima.

2026-02-18: Design doc drafted: drive.google.com/file/d/console-telemetry-sanitizer-design (internal). Core design reviewed with Reliability and Observability teams; agreed on provenance header schema and replay topic semantics.

2026-02-25: Prototype: implemented detector as gRPC interceptor with zero-config fallback (samples only). Local load tests show +3ms p50 overhead; memory allocation within target. Pushed experimental branch: github.com/redwood-inference/console-ingest/pull/3124.
2026-03-03: Review feedback from Observability: need per-tenant drift histograms and a debug-mode that captures 1:10000 raw payloads for security audits. Updated design doc and test plan.

2026-03-10: Integration: wired sanitizer rules into runtime-config. Added canary replay job in CI that replays 100k events from last-24h sample into staging. First canary run completed; parity checks found 0.6% divergence (investigating mapping for legacy "region" aliases).

2026-03-12: Working on hardening: adding more unit tests for nested-object flattening and adding an opt-out label for customers who require original-only ingest. Planning rollout window week of 2026-03-22.
